templates_considered: requests_have_timeout (SEC-013): fits the timeout part; template rule is statement.param_bound max 30, which judges an omitted timeout at its 10s default and so passes it. Added a statement.param_required rule for explicit timeout.
external_calls_handle_errors (LOG-010): fits the error-handling part (try around external calls). Its limits note says to add stream.from_request, so I added it.
tls_verification_on (SEC-011): does not fit the ask (TLS, not timeout or error handling). Not used.
approved_vendors_only (VND-001): does not fit the ask. Not used.
no_secrets_in_code (SEC-012): does not fit the ask, but the workspace has a credential in a URL (acme_notify_sms.xs) that it would catch. Mentioned to the customer, not written.

rules.covers: external requests time out within 30 seconds (template rule)
every external request sets a timeout explicitly, since an omitted timeout passes param_bound
external calls sit inside a try block so failures reach error handling

ask_parts_not_covered.part: error handling actually handles the failure (catch branch does something useful, not empty)
retries, circuit breaker or fallback behaviour when a vendor is down
external calls made by MCP servers (ai.external.mcp.*) and db.external.*, which take no timeout

ask_parts_not_covered.why: couldn't tell how: unsure whether webflow.request declares a timeout param, so left it out of param_required (kept in param_bound)

ask_parts_not_covered.part: a vendor being down bringing the whole app down (isolation between endpoints)

assumptions: statement.param_required with param_names timeout is the right way to require an explicit timeout; an omitted timeout is otherwise judged at default 10s and passes param_bound
stream.from_request has a timeout param (template limits text implies it does)
webflow.request is a statement name that exists as written in the template
adding stream.from_request to LOG-010 is in scope of the ask (customer said external API calls)
customer wants both rules in advisory mode, as the template and skill default
workspace_names_used: api.request statements in api/app/shipments/quote_POST.xs, api/app/payments/charge_POST.xs, api/app/payments/fraud_check_POST.xs, api/app/bank_accounts/link_POST.xs, function/acme_get_tracking.xs, function/acme_sync_shipping_rates.xs, function/acme_notify_sms.xs, ai/tool/issue_refund.xs, task/retry_failed_webhooks.xs
try_catch in function/acme_get_tracking.xs (only try block in the workspace)
confusions: The catalogue's templates list external_calls_handle_errors with statements [api.request] only, while its limits text says to add stream.from_request for full coverage. Not clear whether the template should be used as-is or extended; I extended it.

statement.param_bound judges an omitted param at its runtime default, and the 10s default passes a max of 30. The template's SEC-013 therefore does not by itself enforce 'has a timeout set', which the customer asked for. Not obvious from the template summary; I had to read the check description to see it.

statement.param_required says a value equal to the default is not counted as set (timeout = 10). Unclear what happens to a customer who sets timeout = 10 deliberately: the rule would flag it, which may be surprising.
The parse summary output drops the severity line, while -o json keeps it. Did not affect the file but made the summary look incomplete.
Whether a template's rule set should be combined with extra rules in the same policy versus a second policy key is not explained. I kept one key per template and added the extra rule to SEC-013.
wished_for: A template or recipe for 'external calls have an explicit timeout AND error handling' that shows param_bound plus param_required together, since the template alone does not enforce an explicit timeout
A check that the catch branch does something (non-empty, or calls a function, or returns an error), since the most common real failure is an empty or swallowing catch
Clarity on whether webflow.request, stream.from_request and the ai.external.mcp.* statements take a timeout param, and which statements in each check accept it
Guidance on whether to set a timeout explicitly to the default value (10) when the rule forbids it
why_confidence: The two policies parse with no rule warnings and cover the timeout and try-block parts of the ask. They do not cover whether the catch handles the failure, retries, or non-HTTP external calls. I did not run xano policy evaluate (forbidden in this task), so the expected findings are predictions from reading the code, not observed results.
